cases.description: Microsoft's documented breaking-strength example: population variance of ten tool readings
cases.expected_note: Microsoft publishes this example's result as 678.84, alongside VAR.S over the same data as 754.27. Independently derived: mean 1328.6, sum of squared deviations 6788.4, divided by n = 10 = 678.84 (VAR.S divides by n-1 and so gives 754.2667)

cases.description: DIVERGENCE PROBE: the paired case to VARPA -- VAR.P IGNORES text rather than counting it as 0
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's VAR.P page is unambiguous where VARPA's is not: 'Empty cells, logical values, text, or error values in the array or reference are ignored.' Data are 1, 2, 3 with mean 2; squared deviations 1+0+1 = 2, divided by n = 3 gives 0.66667 -> 0.6667. The identical range under VARPA gives 1.25, so the two cases together pin down the coercion rule

cases.description: A logical inside a referenced range is ignored, so only the numbers are used
cases.expected_note: Microsoft documents logical values in a reference as ignored by VAR.P. Data 4 and 8, mean 6, squared deviations 4+4 = 8, divided by n = 2 gives 4

cases.description: One data point has zero population variance
cases.expected_note: Population variance divides by n, so a single point gives 0/1 = 0

cases.description: A range holding only text leaves VAR.P with no data points
cases.expected_note: DERIVED, not quoted: the VAR.P page documents no error condition. Text in a reference is documented as ignored, so n = 0 and the population denominator is zero -- #DIV/0!
